Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings:  
• 28-year-old woman with first-ever left occipital throbbing headache, severity 8/10, onset yesterday, minimal relief with single NSAID dose.  
• No focal neurological signs, fever, neck stiffness, visual changes, nausea, or vomiting.  
• Family history significant for migraines.  

Working diagnosis:  Probable primary headache – migraine without aura. Supported by unilateral throbbing quality, moderate-to-severe intensity, functional impairment, and positive family history.

Considerations (other plausible DDx):  
• Tension-type headache – medium likelihood; lacks bilateral non-pulsatile character.  
• Cervicogenic headache – medium-low likelihood; occipital location and sedentary job; no neck pain reported.  
• Serious secondary causes (intracranial mass, SAH) currently low likelihood but to be reconsidered if red-flag symptoms emerge.

Management:  
• Advise trial of stronger NSAID (specific agent and regimen to be dispensed) taken regularly with food; may combine with paracetamol.  
• Encourage rest, adequate hydration.  
• Safety-net advice: seek urgent review if headache worsens, persists >48 h, or if new symptoms appear (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, neurological deficits).  
• No immediate investigations ordered; review planned if poor response or recurrence.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  General advice on rest, hydration, and appropriate analgesic use provided; broader chronic disease prevention not discussed – not recorded.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Relieve current headache and resume normal work.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not applicable/ not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  None at this stage.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Telephone review advised within 1–2 days if symptoms persist or worsen.

1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood: Unilateral throbbing pain, severity 8/10, family history of migraines, and absence of secondary red-flag signs.
